transcript: Stop having dinner the way you do and do this instead. Put a piece of papaya in the blender, a green apple, two tablespoons of oats and a glass of milk. Blend everything well and have it as your dinner. Papaya contains papain, an enzyme that digests the proteins your body could not process during the day. It cleanses the intestine and reduces abdominal bloating from the very first night. The green apple provides pectin that sweeps residues from the intestinal walls and regulates blood sugar so you do not wake up at midnight feeling hungry. Oats keep you full without heaviness. They release tryptophan that your brain converts into melatonin and help you sleep more deeply. And milk enhances that relaxing effect and provides calcium that your bones absorb while you sleep. Together they deflate the belly, improve nighttime digestion and help you get a restorative sleep. It is light, it is nutritious and your body appreciates it because it does not have to spend the night digesting a heavy meal. When you eat light at dinner your body uses the night to repair instead of digest. That is where tissues regenerate, hormones balance and the liver cleanses itself. Do it every night and in just a few days you will notice the difference. You wake up feeling lighter, less bloated and with more energy save this recipe. But I want you to understand something. Most people do not eat heavy at night because they are hungry. They eat heavy because of stress. Late night snacking is not greed. It is a nervous system looking for calm through food. You eat at 10 at night not because you are hungry but because it is the only way your body knows how to bring down the anxiety of the day. As long as stress keeps calling the shots you will keep eating badly at night even if you know you should not write in the comments. Light dinner if you are going to try it and if you want to calm what pushes you to eat at night. I have spent more than 20 years quietly learning how to do it and everything I know is inside the road back to calm. The link is in my profile.
